name: Nephrogenic Systemic Fibrosis

criteria.description: History of renal insufficiency or failure
Symmetric skin induration and thickening predominantly affecting extremities
Skin biopsy showing increased dermal fibrosis with CD34-positive spindle cells and collagen deposition
History of exposure to gadolinium-based contrast agents
Exclusion of systemic sclerosis and other autoimmune fibrosing disorders

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of renal dysfunction, characteristic skin thickening, and confirmatory histopathology
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of scleroderma and other fibrosing conditions.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Symmetric indurated skin plaques with woody texture
Skin thickening predominantly on distal extremities
searchTerms: skin thickening on hands and feet
hard skin on fingers and toes

pathognomonic.symptomName: Restricted joint mobility due to skin fibrosis
searchTerms: limited joint movement from skin tightening
stiff joints due to skin scarring
reduced joint flexibility from skin fibrosis
darkening of skin in affected areas

common.symptomName: Muscle weakness secondary to joint contractures
searchTerms: reduced muscle strength from joint problems
persistent exhaustion due to health problems
weakness or pain in hands and feet
nerve damage symptoms in arms or legs

occasional.symptomName: Swelling of the face and trunk
searchTerms: fluid retention in face and trunk

rare.symptomName: Cardiac arrhythmias secondary to myocardial fibrosis
searchTerms: abnormal heart rhythms from heart tissue damage

rare.symptomName: Pulmonary fibrosis with restrictive lung disease
searchTerms: stiff lungs due to pulmonary fibrosis

laboratory: Elevated serum creatinine indicating renal impairment
Absence of specific autoantibodies (ANA, anti-Scl-70 negative)
imaging: MRI may show skin thickening and fibrosis
Radiographs may reveal joint contractures without erosions
other: Skin biopsy with increased dermal collagen and CD34-positive fibrocytes
History of gadolinium-based contrast agent exposure in patients with renal failure

distinguishingFeatures: Raynaud phenomenon common in systemic sclerosis but absent in NSF
Visceral organ involvement more prominent in systemic sclerosis
Papular mucinous skin lesions rather than indurated plaques
Histopathology shows mucin deposition instead of fibrosis

redFlags: Rapidly progressive skin thickening in a patient with renal failure
History of recent gadolinium-based contrast exposure
Development of joint contractures limiting mobility
references: Marckmann P, Skov L, Rossen K, et al. Nephrogenic systemic fibrosis: suspected causative role of gadodiamide used for contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging. J Am Soc Nephrol. 2006;17(9):2359-2362.
Cowper SE, Robin HS, Steinberg SM, Su LD, Gupta S, LeBoit PE. Scleromyxedema-like cutaneous diseases in renal-dialysis patients. Lancet. 2000;356(9234):1000-1001.
High WA, Ayers RA, Chandler J, et al. Gadolinium is detectable within the tissue of patients with nephrogenic systemic fibrosis. J Am Acad Dermatol. 2007;56(1):21-26.
